variant: Boeing 737-800 with blended winglets (737-800W), CFM56-7B, clean, gear down, static on ground
status: exterior-reference-reviewed; visual acceptance pending owner review

references.title: 737NG Airplane Characteristics for Airport Planning, D6-58325-7 Rev C, October 2025
references.author: Boeing
references.license: Public manufacturer document; local study only, no diagram pixels redistributed
references.scope: 2.2.6 general dimensions, 2.3.3 ground clearances, 2.5.1 cross section, 2.7.1 and 2.7.5 door drawings. Line art is vector and was read numerically. Section 4.4 visibility figure: pilot eye 2.49 m aft of the nose tip, 0.51 m off the centerline, 3.74 m high; 15 degrees down and 18 up through the main window.

references.title: KLM 737-800 PH-BGB taxiing, pics 2 and 3
references.author: Alf van Beem
references.license: Public domain; reference only, no pixels embedded
references.scope: Oblique ground views: fin height, windshield extent, nacelle lip, exposed main wheels. Airline livery ignored.

calibration: Vector page units: 0.6590 m/unit along the body from 39.47 m, 0.9285 m/unit vertically from 12.55 m, which also return 4.06 m body depth (published 4.01). Heights are then rebased to the annotated tables.

comparisons: Side and top renders overlaid with the ACAP vector outlines: plan agrees within line width; nose, crown, keel, wing and winglet lie on the drawing.
Three-quarter render inspected beside the KLM photographs. No matched-camera overlay was made.
corrections: Generic needle nose replaced: body depth 2 m aft of the nose is now 2.90 m against 1.22 m in the generic body.
Stance from sills: 2.74 m forward and 3.12 m aft over 26.4 m is 0.82 degrees nose down; crown-to-floor 2.49 m from 2.5.1 reproduces 5.23 m forward and the tabulated 5.56 m aft.

General arrangement draws the fin 7.6 m above the crown; tables 2.3.3 leave 6.9 m and the photographs agree, so fin heights are compressed onto the annotated value. Stabilizer tip likewise follows the table.
Windshield extended to u 3.4 from drawing 2.7.1 after the small general arrangement stopped at 2.94.
Seated eye moved from u 3.30 to the published 2.49, and up to h 2.76 (1.21 m over the floor). The old eye sat 0.8 m aft, which is what made the windows look low and the crown hang in the view.
The sill stood at h 2.63 at the nose, level with the eye, where 2.2.6 draws the front pane corner at 2.36. It now crosses the nose at 2.38, so something solid no longer sits dead ahead.

Kit changes: glass clear from the seat and tinted from outside, as on the Bendy airliner. The thick glareshield slab and its large FLIGHT GUIDANCE lettering are replaced by a thin sloped hood with a rolled lip over a slim mode control strip. The panel, floor and overhead take their reach from the nose skin, and a dark coaming lines the inside of the nose.
Published eye stations for four kit types sit 0.8 m ahead of where the kit had put them, and the same bias was removed here.

limitations: Annotated stance is taken 72 percent from MTW to OEW to match the quoted 12.55 m; real attitude varies with load.
Airfoil, wing-body fairing and flap-track shapes are approximate; gear legs are simplified and thinner than the real oleos; gear doors omitted.

The kit's elliptical nose section is rounder than the real faceted windscreen, so the sill at the pilot's line is matched by raising the eye 0.1 m over the drawing rather than by the surface itself. The windscreen reads -17/+22 against the published -15/+18.
Sanity pass only: seating, glass and visibility. The panel, hood and pedestal remain the shared kit interior fitted to the nose, not compared with this type's real flight deck.
